source_title: The 2027 Ineos Grenadier Quartermaster Has the Substance to Back Up Its Land Rover-Esque Style - Car and Driver
source_excerpt:
Land Rover-inspired retro-styling, real-deal towing and payload ratings, baked-in exclusivity.
Wayward steering, disappointing fuel economy, high price of entry.
The Ineos Grenadier Quartermaster pickup isn’t for everyone—and that’s precisely the point.

Ostensibly a mid-size four-door pickup truck, the Ineos Grenadier Quartermaster stretches the definition. Based on the stately Grenadier Wagon , the Quartermaster has a slightly stretched wheelbase and, crucially, a five-foot bed (61.5 inches to be precise) where the wagon—and SUV by any other name—has an enclosed cargo area. The mechanicals are nearly identical, the Quartermaster using the same BMW-sourced 281-hp turbocharged inline-six, eight-speed automatic transmission, solid axles, and four-wheel drive system as the wagon. While its retro-Rover styling could be construed as pretentious, its 1840-pound payload capacity and 7716-pound tow rating tell a different story. Yes, the fuel economy is daunting, and the steering remains vague despite some recent updates , but the Quartermaster knows exactly what it is and who it appeals to, and in that sense it’s without fault.
Expert Tip: The Quartermaster's obvious alternative is the Grenadier Station Wagon; but if having a pickup bed on a trail-eating machine is non-negotiable, check out the Jeep Gladiator , which displays a little visual sass of its own while offering similar towing and payload capacities at a lower price.

The Helmsman is added to the lineup as the most affordable trim. Featuring unique color combos, the Helmsman will be joined by additional special edition models soon. On the other end of the price schedule is the new Fieldmaster Highlands edition. It includes special saddle leather on the steering wheel, handbrake handle, and passenger grab handle, plus heated Recaro seats, premium floor mats, unique alloy wheels, and a few other upscale additions.
If this year's model is largely unchanged and you're comfortable with a lightly used car, you may want to consider shopping previous model years. A one-to-three-year-old model will likely have a warranty and it'll cost less than buying new.
You won't find another off-roader on the trail with a central nervous system like the Quartermaster's. A turbocharged 3.0-liter inline-six from BMW, good for 281 horsepower and 331 pound-feet of torque, mates with an eight-speed automatic transmission and a permanent four-wheel-drive system with a two-speed mechanical transfer case. A locking center differential is standard, but front and rear lockers are also available. Under the body lie two solid axles that are suspended with coil springs at all four corners.
Like the Jeep Gladiator pickup, the Ineos uses recirculating-ball steering rather than a modern rack-and-pinion setup. It takes some getting used to—it feels less precise and requires more corrections—especially if you are familiar with modern electric power steering setups. Think of it as underscoring the vintage feel of this truck.

In Comparison: Although 8.1 seconds may sound pokey, our long-term Jeep Gladiator with the 3.6-liter V-6 and a six-speed manual required 8.5 seconds to do the same. That said, we tested an automatic V-6 Jeep Gladiator Overland, and it proved much quicker at 7.3 seconds. A Grenadier Wagon—the SUV version—also did the 60-mph deed in 7.3 seconds.
The Quartermaster's tow rating matches that of the Grenadier SUV. That’s much better than the Toyota Tacoma and marginally better than the Chevy Colorado’s 7700-pound towing capacity. Unfortunately, the Quartermaster doesn’t come standard with a trailer brake controller.
In Comparison: Interestingly, the Quartermaster's 7,716-pound max tow capacity is just 16 pounds more than the Jeep Gladiator's 7,700-pound max tow rating.
The EPA has given the Quartermaster fuel economy ratings of 14 mpg city, 14 mpg highway, and 14 mpg combined. We'll update this section with data from our 75-mph highway fuel economy test as soon as it's available. For more information about the Quartermaster's fuel economy, visit the EPA's website .
In Comparison: The Jeep Gladiator V-6 earns an optimistic EPA estimate of 17 mpg city and 22 mpg highway, but our long-term Gladiator Mojave V-6 returned 16 mpg overall during its 40,000-mile stay.
First Row: Two comfortable and supportive seats are bisected by a large console that extends vertically up the dashboard. There's plenty of legroom and headroom, but taller folks will be looking through the top of the windshield; sliding the seats fully rearward puts your head in proximity to the B-pillar. The switch-laden console gives off an aeronautical vibe, particularly when combined with the optional overhead switch panel.
Second Row: Though the Quartermaster has four doors like its SUV sibling, rear seat room is limited. The seatbacks are positioned upright, and legroom is almost nonexistent when the front seats are set fully rearward. There's plenty of headroom and shoulder room, however, and dedicated HVAC vents keep passengers comfortable.
Cargo Capacity: Outside of the console and glovebox, there's not a lot of storage room in the cabin. DIYers will be disappointed to learn that there's only 44.8 inches between the wheel housings of the five-foot bed. Reportedly designed to fit the standard Euro pallet, handy stateside buyers will need to be a little creative to haul standard sheet goods.
Connectivity: Bluetooth, wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto
Audio System: 4-speaker stereo (standard), 5-speaker stereo with subwoofer (optional)
Every Ineos Grenadier Quartermaster comes with a 12.3-inch infotainment touchscreen that can also be operated via a rotary dial. Wireless Android Auto and Apple CarPlay are standard, but the Grenadier doesn’t offer wireless smartphone charging. The optional Premium Audio system consists of a more powerful amplifier and a subwoofer.
There are multiple ceiling-mounted illuminated switches that owners can tap into for accessories such as LED light bars, winches, auxiliary battery power systems, and more. There are single USB-A and USB-C ports in front and a pair of USB-C ports in the rear; two 12-volt power outlets and a household 120-volt outlet add convenience.
All Grenadier models come with a lane departure warning system, automatic emergency braking, speed limit detection, and a driver drowsiness monitoring system.
Standard Safety Features: Automated emergency braking, lane-departure warning, front and rear parking sensors
For information about the Grenadier Quartermaster's crash-test results, visit the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration ( NHTSA ) and Insurance Institute for Highway Safety ( IIHS ) websites.
The Quartermaster is only the second vehicle built by Ineos, and its small dealer network reflects its young age. Every Grenadier frame is covered by a 12-year perforation warranty and a longer limited warranty than Jeep, Land Rover, and Mercedes-AMG.
Limited Warranty: five years or 60,000 miles
Powertrain Warranty: five years or 60,000 miles
